evidence.quote: Were you approached by community and/or political party representatives?

claims.text: Addressed to the interviewer, this records whether the field team was itself approached by community or party actors around access to the visit, not the respondent's partisanship or influence.

evidence.quote: Did you feel threatened during the interview?

claims.text: The referent of the feeling is the interviewer inside this interview encounter, so a positive response expresses felt intimidation rather than any bodily act or the respondent's own fear.

evidence.quote: Were you physically threatened during the interview?

claims.text: This narrows threat to bodily intimidation in the same encounter, so felt threat and physical threat are distinguishable acts that need not coincide.
A three-valued global attribution of respondent candour made by the interviewer, an evaluated demeanour rather than a verified measure of truthful answering.

evidence.quote: must always obey the laws and the courts

claims.text: A forced choice between presidential exemption from law and courts and obligatory obedience, yielding an abstract constitutional stance rather than a verdict on a named ruling.
A general norm toward military entry into politics, paired against legitimate takeover amid abuse; it is principle-level endorsement, not judgment on a specific coup.
Oversight of MPs is posed as a normative allocation among president or executive, parliament or council, party, voters and no one, not a report that any overseer acted.
The presidential counterpart reuses the same fixed option set, so any office-to-office difference is measurable only within those offered categories.

evidence.quote: she will be criticized, called names, or harassed

claims.text: A likelihood rating about a hypothetical woman candidate's reception by the community, an anticipated social reaction rather than reported harassment.

evidence.quote: should government and elected officials be doing more

claims.text: Requests a desired direction and amount of state effort on women's rights relative to current action, an evaluative demand rather than proof of deficient effort.

evidence.quote: most important for our government and society to address

claims.text: A single top-priority pick among listed rights concerns, so the field records a capped ranking and not independent salience for each concern.

evidence.quote: using the police and security forces to enforce public health mandates

claims.text: Justification is conditional on a health emergency and about a possible measure, so agreement endorses a hypothetical policing power rather than describing enforcement that occurred.

evidence.quote: Who do you think sent us to do this interview?

claims.text: Records the respondent's belief about survey sponsorship across distinct options such as party, government, research company and God; misattribution remains possible and it is no audit of the actual commissioning body.

evidence.quote: Willing to participate in follow-up surveys

claims.text: Stated willingness to be recontacted carries a separate not-applicable category for respondents without a mobile number, so it cannot be read as plain refusal versus consent across all respondents.

inquiries.question: Does felt threat during the interview track bodily threat and low assessed candour within the same encounters, or do interviewer-side experiential, bodily and demeanour reports diverge?
inquiries.alternatives: If felt threat without physical threat co-occurs with 'misleading' candour, threat reads as relational unease shaping credibility judgment; if felt threat is confined to physical-threat encounters, the two items collapse into one safety indicator and the demeanour item stands apart; a pattern where only physical threat aligns with distrust supports an incident-based account rather than dispositional suspicion.
inquiries.ceiling: Interviewer-administered items with no interviewer identifier in the selected fields, so interviewer composition and clustering cannot be separated from encounter variation; no respondent-side threat measure and no verification of true candour; nominal-only associations, no causal or distributional conclusion.
inquiries.route: S04 existing observation-scope and asked-eligible RAW owner; only after source route, design and roles qualified.

inquiries.question: Do respondents assign the same overseer to MPs and to the president, or does the office change who is named as responsible?
inquiries.alternatives: Shared option sets permit stable allocation across offices (an agency logic independent of office) versus office-specific allocation, for example executive oversight of MPs paired with voter oversight of the president; asymmetric naming would show the normative allocation is tied to the office rather than to a general accountability principle.
inquiries.ceiling: Normative 'should' judgments with no observation of actual oversight; no routing evidence that both items were asked of the same respondents in sequence; cross-office comparison bounded by the five substantive categories and no open other.
inquiries.route: S04 existing observation-scope and asked-eligible RAW owner; only after source route, design and roles qualified.

inquiries.question: Does a respondent who sees community harassment of women candidates as likely also demand more state effort and name gender-based violence as top priority, or do these judgments come apart?
inquiries.alternatives: A consistent account has anticipated backlash, higher demanded effort and violence priority moving together; divergence, such as high harassment likelihood with 'about the right amount' or a non-violence priority, would show anticipated social reaction is not a proxy for policy demand; priority is a capped single pick, so a different named issue does not mean violence is unimportant.
inquiries.ceiling: Hypothetical and evaluative items; no routing evidence that Q51B was unconditioned or that all three were asked of all respondents; no behavioural or distributional claim; salience for unselected concerns is not established.
inquiries.route: S04/I03 catalog joint then R14–16 if independently qualified roles and selected inquiry; candidate only

holds.missing: No interviewer identifier or visit-level record among the selected fields; interviewer attributes appear only as locator candidates.
holds.why: Threat and candour reports cannot be attributed to particular interviewers or separated from interviewer composition effects on the cited fields alone.

holds.missing: No wave, country or date field among the selected items, and bracketed office and place names remain unresolved placeholders.
holds.why: The constitutional referents and the emergency or gender module context cannot be fixed, so cross-national and across-time comparability of these normative items stays undetermined.

holds.missing: No routing or skip documentation showing whether the gender-module items were asked of all respondents and whether Q51B was conditioned on any prior answer.
holds.why: Whether the priority choice is an unconditioned response or a routed subsample cannot be established.

holds.missing: No administrative record of the true commissioning body and no record of later recontact attempts among the selected fields.
holds.why: Observed sponsor attribution cannot be validated against actual sponsorship, and stated follow-up willingness cannot be checked against later participation.
